blurb: Vintage Vegas in the Plaza's glass dome — martinis, bone-in ribeyes, mob stories.

title: Leon's Oyster Shop
subtitle: Charleston, SC
blurb: Char-grilled oysters and fried chicken in a converted body shop.

title: Snow's BBQ
subtitle: Lexington, TX
blurb: Tootsie Tomanetz's Saturday-only pits — Texas Monthly's #1, sold out by 10am.
overview: Snow's BBQ is a renowned Texas barbecue restaurant located in the small town of Lexington roughly an hour outside of Austin, Texas to the east. Snow's is open only on Saturdays from 8 AM until they run out of meat, often around noon. The unusual hours were originally kept to take advantage of a weekly Saturday livestock auction nearby at 12:30 PM. The name comes from owner Kerry Bexley's lifelong nickname.

title: Dooky Chase's
subtitle: New Orleans, LA
blurb: Leah Chase's gumbo z'herbes fed presidents and the movement alike.
overview: Dooky Chase's Restaurant is a restaurant in Tremé neighborhood of New Orleans that in the 1950s and 1960s was known as a place for civil rights leaders to safely "meet and strategize." In 2018, Food & Wine named it one of the 40 most important restaurants of the past 40 years. In 2025 the restaurant was named one of America's Classics by the James Beard Foundation.

title: Skylight Inn BBQ
subtitle: Ayden, NC
blurb: Chopped whole hog with crackling mixed in, under the little Capitol dome.
overview: Skylight Inn BBQ is a barbecue restaurant in Ayden, North Carolina. Founded by Pete Jones in 1947, it specializes in whole hog barbecue.

title: Fore Street
subtitle: Portland, ME
blurb: Wood-fired everything and the open kitchen that made Portland a food destination.
overview: Fore Street is a restaurant at 288 Fore Street in the Old Port neighborhood of Portland, Maine, United States. Owned by Dana Street and Sam Hayward, the restaurant opened in 1996. It was named one of Gourmet magazine's top 50 restaurants in the United States in 2002, being placed 16th on the list. Its former chef Hayward was named the top chef in the Northeastern US in 2004 by the James Beard Foundation.

title: Faidley's Seafood
subtitle: Baltimore, MD
blurb: Jumbo lump crab cakes eaten standing at Lexington Market since 1886.
overview: Faidley's Seafood is a seafood restaurant in Lexington Market in Baltimore, Maryland. It is one of the oldest restaurants of its kind in the Chesapeake Bay area. The restaurant is known for its lump crab cakes.

title: Jack Fry's
subtitle: Louisville, KY
blurb: Bourbon-era supper club energy; shrimp and grits worth the drive.

title: Taquería El Milagro
subtitle: Chicago, IL
blurb: Pilsen's tortilleria-backed steam-table tacos, cheap and correct.

title: Superiority Burger
subtitle: New York, NY
blurb: The veggie burger that made carnivores queue around the block in the East Village.

reception.summary: Pete Wells, in a review of the original location published by The New York Times, awarded the restaurant two of four stars. He praised the yuba cheesesteak as "an honest variation" on the Philadelphia cheesesteak. Writing for Observer, Joshua David Stein compared the restaurant's burger favorably to the chicken sandwich served by Fuku, a restaurant run by David Chang.

quotes.text: Pete Wells, in a review of the original location published by The New York Times, awarded the restaurant two of four stars.

overview: Superiority Burger is a vegetarian burger restaurant located in the East Village neighborhood of New York City. The restaurant opened in its first location in 2015, and was closed from late 2021 until early 2023, at which point it opened in a second, larger location.

title: Mister Jiu's
subtitle: San Francisco, CA
blurb: Michelin-starred Cantonese in a grand Chinatown banquet hall.

reception.summary: Six months after the opening, the restaurant earned its first Michelin star in October 2016, becoming the first Chinese restaurant in San Francisco to do so, and has retained it since. As of December 2023, the restaurant remains the only Chinese restaurant in the United States with just one Michelin star.

overview: Mister Jiu's (Chinese: 周先生; pinyin: Zhōu xiānsheng) is a Michelin-starred Chinese restaurant in Chinatown, San Francisco. It specializes in Cantonese cuisine blended with modern Californian twists.

title: Night + Market Song
subtitle: Los Angeles, CA
blurb: Kris Yenbamroong's party-Thai — larb, natural wine, and zero chill.
overview: Night markets or night bazaars (Chinese: 夜市) are street markets which operate at night and are generally dedicated to more leisurely strolling, shopping, and eating than more businesslike day markets. The culture of night markets originates from China and have spread globally with overseas Chinese populations.

title: Staplehouse
subtitle: Atlanta, GA
blurb: Nonprofit-born tasting counter that became Atlanta's toughest reservation.

reception.summary: Staplehouse received one Michelin star, denoting "high-quality cooking". A review in The Infatuation noted the restaurant's "cheery" courtyard, praising Staplehouse's family-friendly nature.

overview: Staplehouse is a restaurant in Atlanta, Georgia, United States. The restaurant received a Michelin star in 2024, though they lost it the next year in 2025 because they stopped offering their dinner tasting menu.

title: Le Pigeon
subtitle: Portland, OR
blurb: Gabriel Rucker's chef's counter — foie gras profiteroles, no apologies.

reception.summary: Brooke Jackson-Glidden included the foie gras profiteroles in Eater Portland's 2024 overview of "iconic" Portland dishes. Katrina Yentch included Le Pigeon in the website's 2025 overview of the best restaurants in Buckman. Rebecca Roland included the foie gras profiteroles in Eater Portland's 2025 overview of the city's eleven best restaurants for desserts.

overview: Le Pigeon is a French bistro in Portland, Oregon's Buckman neighborhood, in the United States.

title: Owamni
subtitle: Minneapolis, MN
blurb: Sean Sherman's decolonized menu — bison, wild rice, and zero colonial ingredients.

reception.summary: On opening, recognition came from local, national, and international reviewers. Less than one year after opening, Owamni won the James Beard Foundation Award for best new restaurant in 2022.

overview: Owamni by the Sioux Chef, or simply Owamni, is a Native American restaurant in downtown Minneapolis, Minnesota, that overlooks the Mississippi River. Owamni's majority Native American staff serves a menu made from indigenous ingredients such as game meats, corn, and wild plants.

title: The French Laundry
subtitle: Yountville, CA
blurb: Thomas Keller's nine-course benchmark — the reservation is the flex.

reception.summary: Since 2006, it has been awarded three stars in the Michelin Guide to San Francisco. It received a favorable review in The New York Times and was called "the best restaurant in the world, period" in 2005 by restaurateur and celebrity chef Anthony Bourdain. Since 2007, the restaurant has been the recipient of the Wine Spectator Grand Award.

quotes.text: It received a favorable review in The New York Times and was called "the best restaurant in the world, period" in 2005 by restaurateur and celebrity chef Anthony Bourdain.

overview: The French Laundry is a three-Michelin star French and Californian cuisine restaurant located in Yountville, California, in Napa Valley. Sally Schmitt opened The French Laundry in 1978 and designed her menus around local, seasonal ingredients; she was a visionary chef and pioneer of California cuisine. Since 1994, the chef and owner of The French Laundry is Thomas Keller.

title: Chez Panisse
subtitle: Berkeley, CA
blurb: Alice Waters' farm-to-table origin point, still setting the menu daily.

reception.summary: In 2001, Gourmet magazine named Chez Panisse the Best Restaurant in America. From 2002 to 2008, it was ranked by Restaurant magazine as one of the top 50 restaurants in the world and was ranked number 12 in 2003. Michelin awarded the restaurant a one-star rating in its guide to San Francisco Bay Area dining from 2006 through 2009, but the restaurant lost its star in 2010.

overview: Chez Panisse is a restaurant in Berkeley, California, known as one of the originators of California cuisine and the farm-to-table movement, opened and owned by Alice Waters. The restaurant emphasizes ingredients rather than technique and has developed a supply network of direct relationships with local farmers, ranchers, and dairies.
